Wording and code match the grade 4 cell (page 25; stem and parts a to c). Changed condition: parts a and b describe the text by one compound word that says only that it is at level and names no owner of that level; under grade-level standards the usual reading is the level of the grade. The summary makes it the level of the child, and Limits says outright that the texts are at the level of the child personally and that the statement does not define it. The official text does not say the level is the individual child's; a designer would read this as texts matched to each reader. Keep the summary to what the statement says (text at level, undefined) and take the owner out of Limits. Place: the script put this record at offset 68 on page 25, which is the grade 3 cell of the same row with the same words; the grade 4 cell starts at offset 169.

Wording and code match the cell (page 35; stem and parts a to d, in order). Round 2, after the fix. Read in number 1 of the grade 4 column on PDF page 35 (page image, the opening line also at 300 dpi): opening line and parts a to d in order, nothing else in the cell, no boldface. Code equal. The fix resolved the round 1 reason: the Summary's sentence on part d no longer gives a time for going back over the ideas. Form: the record's line for part d has no space between the letter label and the first word, as in the export; the PDF prints the space and the words are equal. Noted, not counted: the Summary and Limits name the group as the party that agreed the rules, where the statement says only that the rules are agreed; the example under In a child's hands places the child's closing remark at the end of the talk, as an illustration and not as part of the statement.

Compared by eye in number 3 of the grade 4 column, Speaking and Listening table, PDF page 35 (also at 300 dpi). One word differs: the eighth word of the statement. The record, as imported from the export, has a two-letter preposition there; the adopted PDF prints the two-letter conjunction that joins the two kinds of source (the two words differ in their second letter). The PDF reading is the grammatical one, so the export has a typing error. Everything else is equal, including the closing California mark, and nothing else stands in the cell. The summary already follows the PDF reading. California addition, as the PDF boldface shows it: the eighth to tenth words (the joining word and the second kind of source) and the mark. For the fixer: Limits says what the stored wording reads and how the summary takes it; it can now say that the adopted PDF prints the joining word, and it quotes four words of the official wording where a description would do. The record itself can only be right when the importer may correct the export from the PDF.

Round 2. The wording is now right: it is the export's as corrected from the adopted document at one place (one word, an export typing error: the eighth word of the statement), and it equals number 3 of the grade 4 column on PDF page 35 word for word (page image, also at 300 dpi), with the closing California mark; nothing else stands in the cell. The correction is right, and the round 1 reason (wording-differs) is resolved. Boldface on the page: the eighth to tenth words and the mark. Code equal. The Summary is faithful to the corrected wording. What is wrong now is Limits. Its third and fourth sentences, written by the fix round before the importer's correction, still say that the stored wording has a two-letter preposition as its eighth word, that the adopted document prints a conjunction in that place, and that the summary follows the document's reading. The stored wording now has the conjunction, exactly as the adopted document does, so these sentences describe a defect the record no longer has and contradict its wording. For the fixer: remove the two sentences, or replace them with one that says the wording is the export's, corrected from the adopted document at one word. The rest of Limits (the two kinds of source, no judging asked, the California mark that does not show how much was added) is right.

Round 3. The round 2 reason is resolved: the two Limits sentences that described a defect the stored wording no longer has are gone, and one sentence now says that the wording is the export's as corrected from the adopted document at one word. That is what the importer's list holds for this code (one correction, the eighth word, an export typing error), and it is right on the page image (PDF page 35, grade 4 column, number 3). The wording equals the cell word for word, with the closing California mark; nothing else stands in the cell. Code equal. Read whole: the Summary is faithful (the two things to be identified; either kind of source; as backing for the points made; identifying, with no judging). Its shape, recorded and not counted a fault: one sentence that keeps the statement's order of parts; about six in ten of the statement's words recur in order, all of them its terms with their articles; every other word is the pack's, the two things identified stand in the other order, and the longest shared run is three words. Other confirmed one-sentence summaries of this lane are as close or closer, so it is not a near copy by the measure the lane was checked with; if the short summaries of the lane are ever recast, this is one to start with. Limits right: the two kinds of source, no judging asked, and the mark that does not show how much was added (boldface on the page: the eighth to tenth words and the mark).
